pr_title: Enable transitions only for kasa-branded tplink devices
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Disable support for transition for tapo-devices, which do not allow defining it for individual calls.
Users could emulate changing transitions by chaning the device settings using exposed "smooth transitions" & "smooth on" and "smooth off" entities.

Marking as draft as this will require adding tests and perhaps even finding a nicer way to detect the support for transitions.

In addition to the comment above regarding a `supports` check being added to the light interface for this, we may also want to consider actually adding transition support to the library for `smart` devices. It should be fairly straight forwards to wrap the the functions with a `transition` decorator that checks the `get_on_off_gradually` values beforehand, sets them as necessary, and then resets them back afterwards.

We can revisit this later when we have a way to signal about supported (module) features, so I just removed the branch for now. 

@sdb9696 I also had the very same idea earlier, but I think I'd rather avoid making implicit, persistent configuration changes as they have a tendency to cause odd issues when something goes wrong before reverting back to the earlier configuration.

issue_context.title: TP Link L530 bulbs not transitioning properly
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When I call the light.turn_on service on by TP link Tapo L530 bulbs, they ignore any transition instructions. I am able to successfully transition another light using the same integration which is a Kasa KL135 bulb, however the L530's are not transitioning as expected.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.7.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

TP-Link Smart Home

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tplink

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
service: light.turn_on
data:
  brightness_pct: 2
  transition: 22
  rgb_color:
    - 245
    - 20
    - 20
target:
  device_id: fa23ed54be01ee6dbb2d608ea92f2638
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

Alas, only kasa-branded devices support defining a transition for individual commands, so we should remove the transition from supported features for tapo bulbs like yours.

For tapo devices, you can either toggle smooth transitions on and off, or adjust the transition time for both on & off separately. You could use a script to adjust those values prior adjusting the light settings to simulate different transition periods.

I'm having the same issues with L530 bulbs 2 off.
But I've working with Tapo as well over them dropping off the network with 2 issues I have
1 when powering off and back on they come on as 100% white
2 sometimes they lose there programs in the Tapo app on at sunset and off at set times.
Tapo is causing issues in HA on timeouts.
It did do an update 2 days ago but no different. 
Update - 2 bulbs above are hardware 1 - a 3rd L530 I have is hardware 2 and don't seem to have the issue.

review_comments:
I think it would be better to implement this in the library similar to how it's done for the [`energy` interface](https://github.com/python-kasa/python-kasa/blob/master/kasa/interfaces/energy.py#L17) rather than using credentials as a proxy.

Also if we are going to comment on device types probably better to refer to them as the newer `smart` models as this would affect kasa products as well, e.g. ks240.
Agreed, it'd be much nicer to have some way to signal about supported (module) features :+1:
